stories.caption:
我没有动人的故事，我只有对水磨石的执着。

我不想再被自己的负面声音困住。

我想记住的不是自己的怀疑，而是这一件事：

2026 年，Shí 开始让 terrazzo 离开地面，漂浮在光里。
。
。
My second year stepping into the art world has been filled with uncertainty and self-doubt.

Over the past few years, I’ve seen many incredible works. Some artists transform their life experiences into art. Some draw inspiration from their life moments, turning it into something entirely new.

As I listened to them share their stories, I kept asking myself:

What about me?

My story didn’t seem as moving.

Celestial Drift wasn’t born from something personal. It simply came from something much simpler, my desire to challenge the way people perceive terrazzo, my desire to reimagine terrazzo.

I’ve always believed terrazzo could become so much more than what we know it to be. It doesn’t have to stay on the ground. It doesn’t have to remain an architectural material. I simply wanted to see how far I could push its possibilities.

But I kept wondering…

Is that enough?
Would people understand it?
Would they like it?

When the piece was finally completed, I was genuinely proud of it.

I remember thinking,

“I did it. I’ve taken another step forward.”

Yet when it came time to write the artist statement, I froze.

I thought my story wasn’t powerful enough.

After struggling for quite some time, I eventually wrote the truth.

There wasn’t an inspiration. There wasn’t an emotional turning point.

There was only my curiosity.
My stubbornness.
My unwillingness to accept that terrazzo had already reached its limits.

Now, I want to be kinder to myself.

I don’t want to let my own doubts overshadow what I’ve created.

Instead, I want to remember this:

In 2026, Shí let terrazzo leave the ground and drift into the light.
